I just picked the game up again after not playing it for awhile. I seem to recall having beat all of the original villains except for citizen dawn, but I might be wrong.

I've tried twice now to defeat omnitron (with three heroes, using the updated errata). But each time I lost, and the last game was purely and simply a diseaster. I think I only managed to reduce his hit points to like 88 before all three of my heroes were incapacitated. He kept pulling sedative flechettes over and over again, which I found to be really annoying. And what's really ironic is I found what I wasn't even playing the game right. When his brought a drone out at the end of his turn I didn't bother using its end-of-turn effect since it just came out right at the end of the villain turn.

The first game I used Tempest, Wraith, and Bunker. I lost bc he got out adapative armor plating, then tempest was incapacitated and the other two heroes were unable to do anything to him since they both only deal projectible damage. Second time I thought hard on what champions I should use. I went with tempest, Absolute zero, and tachyon. I chose tachyon bc she's the only deck that doesn't really heavily on ongoing and equipment cards. This time, I chose to flip omnitron on the first turn (since the card does say to do that, and it gives no indication you're not supposed to on the first turn, and besides that I thought it might make it easier on me). Right after Zero got his two main equipment out, he pulled a technological singularity (which he didn't do the first game, though he pulled the sedatives at least four or five times, imagine my surprise when I found out that there was only 2 in his deck), which besides taking out a huge chunk of his already diminished hitpionts set him back two more turns. Omnitron btw managed to take my heroes down to about half within 3 or 4 turns. Mostly bc he pulled sedatives twice in a row on either his first or second turn.

I used the insula primalis environment on both games. I actually spent more time fighting the environment deck the first game than I did omnitron. Second game it was as bad, though a couple of t-rexs took out a good chunk of Zero's hit points.

How is it possible to beat this guy? I can't fathom why he's given the same difficulty rating as baron blade in the enhanced rule book (warlord voss is easy compared to omnitron). All his cards are insanely powerful, I mean seriously h+1 damage to all heroes AND destroys all their ongoing cards, seriously? And singularity pretty much renders all equipment-heavy heroes completely useless (assuming he pulls it anyway, wraith actually did fairly well the first game). And that's not even counting the desintigration ray, and the electro-magantic railgun, and the adaptive plating, and the interpolation beam, oh and let's not forget the electro-pulse explosive, which at least will deal 10 damage to everyone on the next villain turn. And I don't appreciate it when the one drone comes out and heals what little damage I did to omnitron (most of my attacks are spent taking out the drones)

 

How do you beat this guy? I see no way to do it, his deck has at least one card that completely counters every hero there is!

Um, if I am not mistaken, when Omni is on his Self-Aware Robotics Factory side, you don't shuffle his trash into his deck: you just shuffle the trash, full stop. Meaning you put the cards in the trash face down so you can't seem it, shuffle them, then reveal cards from the top to put into play, putting the rest of the trash back in the, er, trash.

Also, I would suggest using heroes like Tachyon who don't rely on having stuff on the board. Other good ones would be Visionary. I find Fanatic to be very effective for some reason (Final Dive and Wrathful Retribution maybe?), especially in environments like IP where +damage is commonplace. Tempest is another good call (Knock that Electro-Pulse to the Stratosphere!).

Any hero with redirection (true redirection, not "getting hit then hitting someone else back for that much damage") is also very, very useful against the EPE. Choose to be the first to be hit by the Explosive, redirect it back at it (destroying it), and saving everyone else around you in the process. Yey! Tachyon and NightMist are perfect for this job :)

I consider Omnitron slightly easier than Baron Blade, although the swing is most obvious in a 5-player game on Advanced mode…3-player or non-Advanced games are about even I think.  But aside from the several mistakes you've made, some of which have already been pointed out, the bottom line is that Omnitron is very slow, and most of his threats can be counteracteed quickly.  Sedative Flechettes is a wrecking-ball of a card, but he only has two; Technological Singularity and Terraforming are both potentially blank, his Repair Drones only delay the inevitable, all his Drones are easy to kill, his Components (except Interpolation Beam) don't fire until the start of the next turn and are quite easy to destroy before then with any sort of decent damage-dealing party…the only really strong cards in his deck are Flechettes, Electro-Pulse Explosive, and the Adaptive Plating if you don't have a diverse party.  Also the Environment makes a difference; because Omnitron is invariably higher-HP than heroes while his Drones are extremely low, it's common for environment cards that target high or low HP to work in your favor.  (Ones that target second-highest or -lowest HP are more of a problem, of course.)

Above all other heroes, the ultimate wrecking ball to Omnitron is The Visionary.  Precognition and Suggestion on his Factory turns will entirely neuter him by forcing him to play a blank card, and even when he's a Rampaging Robot, he's much less dangerous playing 1 relevant card than 2.  Visi can also use Wrest the Mind to entirely neutralize Electro-Pulse Explosives (when it tries to deal 15 damage to the first of all hero targets, you redirect that damage to itself, it's destroyed, and Visi doesn't even take 3 damage herself because Wrest the Mind was destroyed along with its target); failing that, she can have a weak Drone hit Omnitron and then kill itself instead of hitting a hero.

When his brought a drone out at the end of his turn I didn't bother using its end-of-turn effect since it just came out right at the end of the villain turn.

Since we've established that you weren't supposed to get that many Flechettes, I'd say two wrongs were making a right here.  I once had a game in which I beat Omnitron by accidentally allowing one of his Drones to attack all targets instead of just one…he killed Tachyon, who was right before Unity in the turn order, and Unity's deck is made mostly of extremely powerful robots that are impossible to play on your own turn without jumping through some hoops.  But Tachyon can grant a card play while Incapacitated, and since it's not Unity's turn, she can just plunk down a robot without any difficulty.  Thusly, Tachyon was far more useful dead than alive, and Visionary was also in that game (and we were in Insula Primalis, where the Velociraptors invariably attacked Drones, and the T-Rexes were Wrested by Visionary into attacking Omnitron after having legally done so once, because he had lower HP than the second Tyrannosaur) - nevermind, I'm mixing up a different pair of Visionary games, one with Omnitron and one on Insula, but the time they were both there this did not happen.  (I have had her throw a Monorail car at Omnitron with Wrest the Mind when they were in Metropolis, and I've had her Wrest a Tyrannosaurus once, but that was against Ambuscade.)

he got out adapative armor plating, then tempest was incapacitated and the other two heroes were unable to do anything to him since they both only deal projectible damage.

Bunker does have a few cards that deal other damage types - External Combustion for fire and Omni-Cannon for Energy I believe.  Wraith occasionally does melee (although it is weird, given that her shtick is being Batman, that she hasn't prepared any Equipment that can deal with this problem).  And occasionally the dinosaurs will deal melee damage to him and give you a window to get through the Plating that way, plus the Plating can simply be destroyed with a Grappling Hook or Ball Lightning or something.  But yeah, if Plating comes down against the wrong group of heroes, it's sort of a "You Lose" card unless you luck into the right way around it.  Omnitron has a lot of cards like that, which is part of why Visionary, the ultimate deck-manipulation hero, is such a magic bullet against him.

This time, I chose to flip omnitron on the first turn (since the card does say to do that, and it gives no indication you're not supposed to on the first turn, and besides that I thought it might make it easier on me).

He does indeed flip on the first turn - he technically starts the game as a Factory, but the first thing to happen in every game is that he goes Rampaging and plays two Villain cards.  It'd be pretty silly for him to be a Factory on turn 1 since he'd have no trash to reshuffle in search of a Drone or Component; even as-is, his second-turn first Factory effect is almost always a blank, because if he plays a Drone on turn 1, you probably won't bother to kill it, knowing he'll get it right back.  And if he plays a Component, and you're able to destroy that Component before his next turn so he gets it back…well, then you can probably destroy it again just as easily.  Usually it'll be at least turn 4 of the game before he'll raise anything from his trash.

Right after Zero got his two main equipment out, he pulled a technological singularity

Right, that's a clear example that these games were not destined to go your way.  Sometimes you get the bear and sometimes the bear gets you.  Absolute Zero is one of the worst possible heroes to use against Omnitron for this exact reason - Bunker and Wraith suffer a fair bit if he does TechSing, but Zero in particular needs his Modules to do anything effective.  He has issues against any hero who can destroy Equipment, such as Citizen Dawn or La Capitan, but Omnitron is the only one who adds insult to injury by punishing you for having ever played equipment.  (Yet another reason why Visionary pwns him, as she doesn't have any.  Traveled back in time with nothing but the clothes on her back, and saw no reason to change that after arriving.)

Omnitron btw managed to take my heroes down to about half within 3 or 4 turns.

That's not too unusual for any villain.  The heroes nearly always take somewhat of a beating, but as long as they have 1 HP left, they're still in the game, and even an Incapacitated hero or two continues contributing with their flipside abilities.  It's very common to have all the heroes down to 5 or 10 on the last turn of the game; it still doesn't mean that was even a particularly difficult fight.  The game's balance point assumes that the heroes will knock down the villain's 50-100 HP (there are four exceptions to this range) at about the same speed that they deplete their own 25-30 HP (three exceptions there, more if you count promo heroes), due to the Villain's attacks as well as their own self-damage effects, with the Environment periodically messing with both sides.

I can't fathom why he's given the same difficulty rating as baron blade in the enhanced rule book (warlord voss is easy compared to omnitron).

Here you're just plain incorrect.  You were playing Omnitron all wrong as has been established; played properly, he might be slightly harder than Blade, based on what others on this forum have told me, but my personal experience is that he's easier (the only time he's beaten me, it was largely due to a particularly nasty Environment, coupled with my getting lazy and overconfident).  And Warlord Voss is probably the toughest of the original four villains, although an argument for Citizen Dawn could be made instead; I'm a bit biased because I just enjoy her more, but I still think Voss is tougher just by virtue of his brutal efficiency, coupled with the virtually unstoppable threat of Forced Deployment, the ability for Gene-Bound Guards to protect the rest of his army (who are admittedly quite squishy otherwise), and the fact that unlike with Dawn, it's completely impossible to ignore the army and just focus fire on him in order to end the game quickly.  (If Dawn flips, you have to deal with the Citizens, but otherwise you can take out the most dangerous few of her initial Citizens, and then leave a relatively harmless one like Spring or Autumn in play, just to keep Dawn from flipping, and then just beat on her nonstop and hope the worst of the Citizens don't show up.)

All his cards are insanely powerful, I mean seriously h+1 damage to all heroes AND destroys all their ongoing cards, seriously?

That is definitely one of the most absurd cards in the game, no argument there.  But look at how wimpy Automaton Drone is in a 3-player game (compare to the Blade Battalion, which are identical to a H=5 version of the Automatons, regardless of the actual H value).  Assault Drones are always a squishy 4 HP and deal just 2 damage to one hero, unless other Drones are out, which will seldom be true because you can keep killing them off (if it were up to me, Omnitron would reanimate ALL his killed Drones every couple of turns, just to get the "robot revolution" flavor to really come through and make it a more sporting battle).  Interpolation Beam is forgettable for most heroes unless you play on Advanced, and half the time even then; the other Components all wait until the start of Omnitron's turn to fire, and are usually easy to blow up before then by dealing 7 damage.  Omnitron is very swingy in terms of his card power, which is one of the reasons he favors a longer game.  If you get lucky on his first few plays, and consistently beat on him hard with a competent damage-dealing party, it's very possible to deprive him of even that massive 100 health before he can stabilize.

oh and let's not forget the electro-pulse explosive, which at least will deal 10 damage to everyone on the next villain turn.

Not true at all.  Even ignoring the Visionary trick I mentioned above, let's look at a party of Haka, Legacy and Absolute Zero (I could go with Ra or Wraith or Bunker instead of Zero, but that would definitely make this a party of above-average deadliness).  The EPE comes out on Omnitron's first turn (along with a Repair Drone or Terraforming or something similarly irrelevant), and then Haka gets a turn; Haka might Elbow Smash the EPE down to 12 and then Crush it to 10, or just put down his Taiaha and bonk the EPE for 3, let's assume the latter so it's left at 12.  Legacy can THOKK! it down to 9, then Galvanize all the heroes.  Absolute Zero plays Isothermic Transducer, then Thermodynamics himself for fire damage; because of Galvanize, the 1 damage is boosted to 2, and then Transduced into 2 damage which is boosted to 3, so he hits the EPE and knocks it down to 6.  That was only a fairly average round, maybe slightly above what a completely random group of heroes with a completely random set of cards might be able to put together, but certainly far short of the deadliest example I could have constructed.  (With five heroes including Legacy, Fanatic and Ra, it'd be far from unusual for the EPE to die halfway through the round and then for Omnitron to lose 10 or so HP thereafter.)

And I don't appreciate it when the one drone comes out and heals what little damage I did to omnitron (most of my attacks are spent taking out the drones)

Repair drones are good.  You want to see repair drones, because they do absolutely nothing to set back the hero team.  They just uptick Omnitron's HP a little; if that's all that ever happened, it would only be prolonging the inevitable.  Aside from Terraforming with no Environments or TechSing with no Equipment, Repair Drone is the most innocuous card in Omnitron's deck, even more harmless than the Components which are only a potential threat.  If you have to spend all your attacks taking out 3-5 HP drones, then your party is well below the median in effectiveness.  If you're stuck playing a group like Chrono-Ranger, Legacy and the Argent Adept (in that order), then yeah, Omnitron is going to be a tough hill to climb.  But even then, the Repair Drones are more of an insult than a threat.  You'll be happy to see them instead of even a mildly dangerous card like the Assault Drone or Interpolation Beam, to say nothing of the actual threats like EPE, Flechettes, or a mid-game Terraforming.

How do you beat this guy? I see no way to do it, his deck has at least one card that completely counters every hero there is!

And what happens when he draws TechSing on turn 1, when even the most equipment-dependent hero hasn't played a card yet?  What happens when he gets Adaptive Plating against a party of Ra, Fanatic, Zero, Haka, and Bunker, where no two of them share a damage type and most of them can do more than one?  Omnitron has very few H variables on relevant cards (Automaton Drone isn't really that dangerous, as it hits only one hero and isn't hard to kill within one round, and the Disintegrator Ray will almost never fire in a high-H game; Flechettes is the only one where it really hurts), so the more heroes you have against him, the easier he is to beat, almost without exception.  You've only done 3-hero games, so the deck was stacked against you, but even so, a careful selection of effective and diverse Heroes (and not making a HUGE rules mistake in his favor) would have easily rendered Omnitron a barely-credible threat.  That, of course, is not really ideal…you want the game to provide some challenge, or what's the fun in bothering to flip all those cards?  So I'd say next time you fight him, grab four random heroes and arrange them in an order that looks optimal, pick a more dangerous Environment like the Ruins of Atlantis (note: Pillars of Hercules or Font of Power into Electro-Pulse Explosives = VERY BAD, but the odds are pretty slim of that happening), and you'll find that he should provide you a good workout without making you feel totally screwed.  If you still manage to lose that game due to bad luck, you then take a party of five including Legacy and Visionary (and excluding AZ), fight in the Wagner Mars Base or on Insula again, and prove to yourself once and for all that he can be beaten, often with embarassing ease.

Here you're just plain incorrect.  You were playing Omnitron all wrong as has been established; played properly, he might be slightly harder than Blade, based on what others on this forum have told me, but my personal experience is that he's easier (the only time he's beaten me, it was largely due to a particularly nasty Environment, coupled with my getting lazy and overconfident).  And Warlord Voss is probably the toughest of the original four villains, although an argument for Citizen Dawn could be made instead; I'm a bit biased because I just enjoy her more, but I still think Voss is tougher just by virtue of his brutal efficiency, coupled with the virtually unstoppable threat of Forced Deployment, the ability for Gene-Bound Guards to protect the rest of his army (who are admittedly quite squishy otherwise), and the fact that unlike with Dawn, it's completely impossible to ignore the army and just focus fire on him in order to end the game quickly.  (If Dawn flips, you have to deal with the Citizens, but otherwise you can take out the most dangerous few of her initial Citizens, and then leave a relatively harmless one like Spring or Autumn in play, just to keep Dawn from flipping, and then just beat on her nonstop and hope the worst of the Citizens don't show up.) > All his cards are insanely powerful, I mean seriously h+1 damage to all heroes AND destroys all their ongoing cards, seriously? That is definitely one of the most absurd cards in the game, no argument there.  But look at how wimpy Automaton Drone is in a 3-player game (compare to the Blade Battalion, which are identical to a H=5 version of the Automatons, regardless of the actual H value).  Assault Drones are always a squishy 4 HP and deal just 2 damage to one hero, unless other Drones are out, which will seldom be true because you can keep killing them off (if it were up to me, Omnitron would reanimate ALL his killed Drones every couple of turns, just to get the "robot revolution" flavor to really come through and make it a more sporting battle).  Interpolation Beam is forgettable for most heroes unless you play on Advanced, and half the time even then; the other Components all wait until the start of Omnitron's turn to fire, and are usually easy to blow up before then by dealing 7 damage.  Omnitron is very swingy in terms of his card power, which is one of the reasons he favors a longer game.  If you get lucky on his first few plays, and consistently beat on him hard with a competent damage-dealing party, it's very possible to deprive him of even that massive 100 health before he can stabilize. > oh and let's not forget the electro-pulse explosive, which at least will deal 10 damage to everyone on the next villain turn. Not true at all.  Even ignoring the Visionary trick I mentioned above, let's look at a party of Haka, Legacy and Absolute Zero (I could go with Ra or Wraith or Bunker instead of Zero, but that would definitely make this a party of above-average deadliness).  The EPE comes out on Omnitron's first turn (along with a Repair Drone or Terraforming or something similarly irrelevant), and then Haka gets a turn; Haka might Elbow Smash the EPE down to 12 and then Crush it to 10, or just put down his Taiaha and bonk the EPE for 3, let's assume the latter so it's left at 12.  Legacy can THOKK! it down to 9, then Galvanize all the heroes.  Absolute Zero plays Isothermic Transducer, then Thermodynamics himself for fire damage; because of Galvanize, the 1 damage is boosted to 2, and then Transduced into 2 damage which is boosted to 3, so he hits the EPE and knocks it down to 6.  That was only a fairly average round, maybe slightly above what a completely random group of heroes with a completely random set of cards might be able to put together, but certainly far short of the deadliest example I could have constructed.  (With five heroes including Legacy, Fanatic and Ra, it'd be far from unusual for the EPE to die halfway through the round and then for Omnitron to lose 10 or so HP thereafter.) > And I don't appreciate it when the one drone comes out and heals what little damage I did to omnitron (most of my attacks are spent taking out the drones) Repair drones are good.  You want to see repair drones, because they do absolutely nothing to set back the hero team.  They just uptick Omnitron's HP a little; if that's all that ever happened, it would only be prolonging the inevitable.  Aside from Terraforming with no Environments or TechSing with no Equipment, Repair Drone is the most innocuous card in Omnitron's deck, even more harmless than the Components which are only a potential threat.  If you have to spend all your attacks taking out 3-5 HP drones, then your party is well below the median in effectiveness.  If you're stuck playing a group like Chrono-Ranger, Legacy and the Argent Adept (in that order), then yeah, Omnitron is going to be a tough hill to climb.  But even then, the Repair Drones are more of an insult than a threat.  You'll be happy to see them instead of even a mildly dangerous card like the Assault Drone or Interpolation Beam, to say nothing of the actual threats like EPE, Flechettes, or a mid-game Terraforming. > How do you beat this guy? Batman isn't really a good name. Wraith on the other hand has a great name.

…

Batman's parents are dead. Wraith's are alive.

He heals instead of taking the damage, though.  He is a bit on the frustrating side, but also has potentially incredible output, if he jumps through all the proper hoops without interference.  Picture this setup:  At the start of his turn, Impale deals 2 damage to a target, which Focused Apertures increases to 3.  He then activates Thermal Shockwave to deal 1 cold damage to each of three targets; the Apertures increase that to 2 each.  So he's dealt a total of 9 cold damage this turn; Thermal Shockwave deals 9 fire damage to him, and Isothermic Transducer turns that into 10 cold damage thanks to the Apertures again.  He can either hit the same target as his Impale and one of the Shockwave hits, making a total of 14 damage that turn, or if he has both modules out, he can have the Transducer "damage" him, enabling him to regain all the HP he lost to the Shockwave and 1 more besides.  (Do note that if the Shockwave damage kills him first, he doesn't get the chance to heal.  This is why Cold Snap plus Shockwave is probably not a good idea, and Cold Snap plus Focused Apertures plus Shockwave is really not a good idea.)

He's heavily reliant on a few specific equipment cards, and buffs from other heroes or the environment.

The former at least is true, he does badly need at least one module to get anything done, and both to work ideally.  But he has four copies of each, plus four copies of the Installation card which searches them out (and lets you draw another card, and if you didn't need to play the Module you searched for you can play a different card instead, so you basically drew one new card without costing yourself anything, as well as trading the Installation for any Module in your deck - do try to count how many are left as you play, though, since you get nothing if they're all in your trash or if you draw the last one before searching).  Buffs from other heroes are not necessary, although they can be amazing - Embolden from Fanatic will let him fire a Coolant Blast after a Thermal Shockwave, dealing a second instance of cold damage equal to the fire damage you took, or it will let you pop Cryo-Chamber for 4 fire damage to yourself before Coolant Blasting for 4+ (although the two aren't normally a great combo; unless you played the Cryo-Chamber that same turn, it cost you a point of fire each time you got hit during the previous round).

Not to mention he pretty much can't do anything until you get set up, I mean seriously his innate power does nothing but damage him

This is why he is one of the heroes most likely to spend his first turn drawing 2 cards.  However he's hardly unique in this - Unity's power does nothing without an Equipment (her own or an ally's) that can be spared and a Golem to turn it into.  Nightmist takes damage to draw cards, which is a painful trade unless she has redirection out.  Argent Adept is useless without a song, Expatriette can do very little without a Gun, Mr. Fixer needs a Tool and a Style…very few characters are as good "out of the box" as Ra and Haka, most of them have to do a fair bit of legwork in order to get rolling, and can be undone badly by a wipe card such as TechSing or Flechettes (or Dawn's Devastating Aurora, which destroys ALL non-villain cards in play, except for Unity's golems or Visionary's Decoy Projection).

Not to mention other heroes (like Ra and Wraith) can easily match his damage output, without damaging themselves

Let me know how often Ra or Wraith can deal 29 damage to one target.  That's the theoretical maximum output of AZ's damage if he does everything exactly right, assuming no external boosts.  (Deal exactly 28 cold damage out including Thermal Shockwave, then Isometric Transducer dishes 29 out thanks to Focused Apertures.)  Fanatic is the only other character that can wallop that hard, and she also ends up at 1 HP afterward (as well as before), but she has only one copy of the triggering card, and must discard 3 cards to use it.

In actual practice, of course, Fanny is probably somewhat better than AZ across the board.  But both are self-damaging heroes, and both give you reasons to damage yourself.  If you can't get the hang of knowing when to let yourself get hurt and when not to, well, maybe these two aren't for you.  But they can definitely be good to have on your team.

and wraith has alot more versatility than Absolute Zero to boot.

Wraith has more versatility than anyone (except possibly Argent Adept, depending on who he's paired with).  If you made a list of the best heroes in the game, it's virtually certain Wraith would be in the top three no matter who was making the list, unless it was purely subjective.  She's a little boring once you "solve" her, but she's just ridiculously good.  Don't criticize other heroes for failing to be The Wraith; they each have their own little niches in which they can shine.

Was he designed to give players a challenge or something?

Among other things.  He's not a handicap, but he is designed to appeal to players who grow bored with the straightforwardness of Ra and Legacy, and want to jump through a few hoops and make themselves look/feel clever.  I'm one of those players, and AZ is in my top third of heroes in the game for precisely this reason…he feels like a puzzle that I enjoy solving.  Though I do think he might not be quite perfectly balanced, as compared to some of the other characters who have similar shticks but seem to execute them a little better (in particular, the other two 3-complexity heroes are both absurdly good when they get a dream setup, compared to which AZ is just okay).

and really the only advantages he does have are immunity to fire

I assume you're talking about using the Transducer to heal himself.  Note that becoming actually immune to fire damage (or to damage in general) is one of the worst things that can happen to him, as it turns off much of his ability to do anything.  This is in flavor for him, since Ryan Frost is a miserable old curmudgeon who does nothing but complain the whole time he's battling to save the world (another reason why I like him, having a similar personality much of the time).  In the words of Garbage, he's "Only Happy When It Rains".  (Tempest can help him with that.)

(sadly though, the villains don't seem to be big on dealing fire or cold damage, most of their damage cards do energy damage)

I agree that this is a little annoying.  Ra also wishes fire damage would get dealt more often, since he can make the entire party immune to it.  A fair number of Environments are fire-centric, but not as many as I'd like.  And I personally find energy damage to be quite unflavorful and unsatisfying (if it were up to me, I'd make most of it into lightning damage, occasionally fire or radiant - the latter type is almost exclusively found on Fanatic and occasionally on The Scholar, and seems to exist mostly as a way to make them feel more special than if they were dealing a "mere mortal" type of damage).

Is there any reason to every play AZ besides for a challenge?

Yes, every reason I stated above.

Focused Apertures in play.  3 cold damage from Impale (needs a target, but you almost certainly have at least one of those, unlike with ongoings and environments), 2 from Cold Snap, 3 from Hoarfire, which deals 3 fire damage to Zero, triggering Isothermic Transducer to deal 4 more cold, then Hoarfire goes on to deal 2 cold (this assumes you do NOT have NPCU in play) and 1 fire to Zero, triggering another 2 cold.  That's 3+2+3+4+2+2=16 outgoing cold damage, then 2 more from Shockwave on a single target, which is 18 outgoing cold damage, so 18 fire damage to Zero which triggers 19 more cold damage.

Any time anything deals damage and gives a number as its damage totals, each given number is a separate instance of damage - Fanatic's Exorcism is one example, of course - she deals one damage and one damage with her base power, therefore any damage boosts (or nerfs) will affect both those totals separately. Another example is Tempest's Vicious Cyclone, which says you can discard up to three cards and deal one damage for each card discarded. So if you are buffed with, say, Galvanise, you'd instead deal two damage for each card discarded.

It's the same with, say, the vats in Pike Industrial - the Supercooled trisolvent Vat deals something like one cold, one toxic, and erm, one something else at the end of the environment turn. If the erm…toxic vat (something-cyclohexane I think it's called…lol sorry bad memory this evening) is out, the one which converts all damage to toxic and increases it by one, the Trisolvent Vat will instead deal two toxic, two toxic, and two toxic damage at the end of the turn.

Compare to cards like Savage Mana, Omni-Cannon, and Lightspeed Barrage, which specify to "…deal X damage, where X is the number of cards…". So you'd total up the damage, and apply any buffs on top of that one total.

Maybe there is another way to frame this discussion. Lets talk about the purpose of "tanking" as it relates to this game. What is "tanking" trying to accomplish? When is the goal of winning the game best served with a tanking approach?

Tanking for me serves one purpose: buying time for the rest of the team to get set up to start doing damage. With the exception of Gloomweaver and possibly Akash (depending on location) there are no real "endurance" test encounters where you just have to bide your time. They are damage races for the most part. Most villains come out of the gate swinging for the fences.

There are a few ways to be an effective tank in this vien. You can redirect damage from others to yourself, or you can manipulate your HP to take the majority of damage instances (those that target the highest HP hero).

AZ lacks the tools to redirect damage to himself from others (like other notable tankers like Legacy or Scholar). Villains that deal a lot of AoE damage are a poor choice for AZ to tank against for this reason. AZ will not be able to mitigate enough damage from the team to warrent the absence of his crazy damage production.

This leaves HP manipulation. Now, AZ lacks any sort of passive mitigation (although Cryo Chamber does mitigate fire damage only). Healing is your only way to achieve any kind of effective mitigation to make tanking worth it, so single target damage heavy villains are a better choice to tank again. But also  keep in mind that there is no real mitigation through healing when your damage in:out ratio is 1:1. It is no good. So you need to be at a higher ratio to get yourself decent mitigation, and at that point your damage is starting to be too good to pass up. And remember any time you heal, you pass up the chance to do damage (the villain is now in effect getting some damage mitigation of his own in that sense).

The question still becomes are you mitigating enough incoming damage to justify the loss of production. Are you really buying the team time to set up? Or are you just stalling and being a burden? This is why he is a complexity 3 hero.
